data.long_meaning: The one who is the ruler and guardian of the sacred path leading to salvation and spiritual enlightenment. data.cultural_impact: The name Vigneshwar is derived from the Tamil language and is an honorific title given to the Hindu deity, Lord Ganesha. In Hindu mythology, Lord Ganesha is known as the remover of obstacles and the patron of wisdom, knowledge, and education. Vigneshwar is also believed to be the lord of the threshold and the guardian of the doorways to temples and homes, making it an auspicious name to invoke for protection, prosperity, and wisdom.
data.spiritual_significance: Vigneshwar is an embodiment of wisdom, knowledge, and power. As the guardian of the spiritual path, he is said to guide and protect those who seek enlightenment and salvation. Vigneshwar represents the removal of obstacles that prevent spiritual growth and the attainment of wisdom and knowledge. In Hinduism, Vigneshwar is also considered the embodiment of the sacred syllable "OM," which is the sound of the universe and the origin of all creation. Hence, invoking the name Vigneshwar provides spiritual strength, guidance, and the removal of inner obstacles towards the path of Self-realization and ultimate salvation.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vigneshwar is the lord of obstacles and difficulties. He is worshipped to remove hindrances and obstacles in life's journey, ensuring the path to success is smooth. Lord Vigneshwar symbolizes the power to overcome challenges and the wisdom to navigate through life's complexities.

historical_references.reference:
According to mythology, Vigneshwar is considered to be the god of obstacles, remover of obstacles and the lord of all creations. He is the patron of the art of sculpture, and the god who blesses us with wisdom, knowledge and wealth. He is also known as the god of promise, grace, and success.
Context: Mythology and Hinduism
Time period: Ancient India

Vigneshwar is also known as Ganesha or Vinayak, the elephant-headed god. He is believed to have been born to the god Shiva and Goddess Parvati to protect her while she was bathing. He is often invoked at the beginning of any new venture or journey to remove any potential obstacles.
Context: Hindu rituals and practices
Time period: Medieval India

trends: God of obstacles and good fortune
modern_usage.modern_context: Vigneshwar, also known as Ganesha or Vinayak, is a popular deity in Hinduism. He is often referred to as the God of obstacles and good fortune, and is traditionally worshipped before starting any new venture or journey to seek his blessings for removing obstacles and ensuring success. In modern times, Vigneshwar is widely revered across various digital platforms including Instagram, Reddit, and YouTube. On Instagram, there are numerous accounts dedicated to the deity, where followers share images, stories, and prayers. On Reddit, there are several communities where devotees discuss rituals, mythology, and share experiences. On YouTube, there are videos of puja rituals, devotional songs, and educational content, providing a platform for devotees to connect and learn about the deity. Overall, Vigneshwar's popularity continues to grow, and digital platforms play an essential role in connecting and engaging the global Hindu community.
